text:
Noah: opened a small focused PR to clarify the Reserved Capacity autoscale section. main goal: make the burst behavior explicit and move runnable snippets into /examples. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4310
Giselle: thanks. can we add a short "quick answer" box at the top: one line that says when we will spill to shared capacity? customers keep skimming docs.
Noah: good idea. drafting: "When reserved pool is saturated, requests follow this fallback order: reserved -> dedicated -> shared; burst capacity has no SLA." will add to the PR.
Tom: on examples: instead of terraform, let's include a CLI and small SDK example. ops teams prefer copy-paste CLI for one-off reservations. CLI draft: `redwood reserve create --name infra-testing --gpus 6 --isolation tenant`
Priya: nit on language in SLA paragraph: please replace vague terms like "best effort" with explicit contract-friendly phrasing: "no SLA for burst capacity" and then list the fallback ordering. avoids legal confusion.
Noah: done 1 added the exact phrasing and a tiny table showing guarantee vs no-guarantee for reserved, dedicated, shared.
Giselle: eviction semantics still confusing for customers. Can we add a single-line pointer to runtime's eviction matrix and summarize: "tenant isolation biases allocation; host-level preemption may still evict workloads."
Tom: infra confirmed that wording. I'll paste the runtime link in the PR comment. also proposed a short eviction priority table (priority: reserved tenant > dedicated > shared) but call out overrides for host pressure.
Noah: adding both the one-line pointer and the small priority row. also extracting CLI + SDK into `examples/reservations/quickstart.md` per earlier doc conventions.
Priya: please include idempotency guidance in SDK snippet (token or request_id). customers copy the simple code and forget retries. small python sample: ```python
from redwood import Client
client = Client(token=REDACTED)
client.reservations.create(name="oncall-temp", gpus=2, isolation="tenant", idempotency_key="req-123")
```
Giselle: also spotted a stale cross-link in the migration guide pointing to `/legacy/terraform` 1 added a suggested replacement to `/migrate/cli-and-terraform`. small redirect in site config will fix it.
doc-bot: generated checklist - add quick-answer line, move runnable snippets to /examples/reservations/, change SLA wording to "no SLA for burst capacity", add eviction matrix pointer, replace stale migration link, include idempotency note in SDK example, paste Console SLO URL into PR comments.
Noah: I'll split the examples, update the migration link, and push the small CLI + SDK files tonight. tagging @Giselle @Priya for review.
Tom: leaving one inline suggestion about consistent use of "reserved pool" vs "reserved capacity". keep terminology single-token.
Giselle: LGTM apart from the terminology nit.
Priya: will review the example file after split. once approved, can someone backport to release-1.3? this is customer-facing.
Noah: yes will request backport after merge. closing thread when PR merges. :rocket:
